passage: I'm Amandeep. When Mum's new friend Jatin came for tea the first time, he brought a box of my favourite jalebis and asked about my robot kit. I said "fine" to everything and went to my room. I was afraid that if I smiled, it would mean Dad could be replaced. Jatin never pushed. The next Sunday he just said hello and asked nothing. I stayed polite, thanked him for the jalebis, and told Mum honestly, "I'm not ready to like him." She hugged me and said that was okay. I am still slow about it, but the knot in my stomach is a little looser now.

qa.q: What did Jatin bring on his first visit?
qa.a: He brought a box of jalebis.

qa.q: Why did Amandeep say "fine" to everything and go to the bedroom?
qa.a: Amandeep was afraid that smiling would mean Dad could be replaced, so Amandeep kept a distance.

qa.q: What did Amandeep do that stayed honest without being rude?
qa.a: Amandeep stayed polite, thanked Jatin, and told Mum truthfully, "I'm not ready to like him."

qa.q: How might Jatin feel when Amandeep goes off to the bedroom?
qa.a: Jatin may feel unsure or a little rejected, but he did not push and simply said hello the next Sunday, which gives Amandeep room.

grounding: A child refuses a mother's new partner out of fear of replacement, stays polite and lets trust come slowly.

passage:
Govind Kaka had started coming to their house in the village every Sunday. He fixed the broken hinge on the cattle shed and brought Lalit a kite. Lalit's mother, Usha, smiled more when he was around.
Lalit left the kite in its paper. He answered Govind Kaka with one word each time. At night he looked at Baba's photo on the wall and felt a tight knot. What if Baba was forgotten?
One Sunday Govind Kaka asked, "Want to fly it together?"
Lalit took a breath. "Not yet. I miss Baba. I don't want anyone to take his place."
Govind Kaka nodded. "Nobody could. We'll go slow."
Lalit said, "Thank you for the kite." He meant it, a little.

qa.a: The broken hinge on the cattle shed.

qa.q: What was Lalit afraid of when he looked at Baba's photo?
qa.a: He was afraid that Govind Kaka would replace Baba and that Baba would be forgotten.

qa.q: What did Lalit do that was honest and still polite?
qa.a: He said plainly that he missed Baba and wasn't ready yet, and he still thanked Govind Kaka for the kite.

qa.q: How might Govind Kaka see Lalit's cold answers?
qa.a: Govind Kaka seems to understand Lalit needs time, saying no one could take Baba's place and they would go slow.

grounding: A boy refuses his mother's new partner's friendliness, fearing he will replace his father, then says so honestly and politely and lets trust grow slowly.

passage:
Every Friday, Sipho arrived at the Johannesburg flat with groceries and a joke for Thabo. Thabo's mum, Amara, laughed at the jokes. Thabo didn't.
When Sipho offered to help with his science project, Thabo said, "Dad always helps me," and shut his bedroom door.
Later he heard Amara and Sipho talking quietly. He felt bad, but also scared. If he liked Sipho, did that mean Dad didn't count anymore?
On Sunday, Thabo came out. "Sipho, I'm sorry I slammed the door. It's just weird. You're not my dad."
"I know," Sipho said. "I'm not trying to be. Maybe just someone who's good at volcano models?"
Thabo almost smiled. "Maybe. Slowly."

qa.q: What project did Sipho offer to help with?
Why did Thabo shut his bedroom door?
qa.a: He felt scared that liking Sipho would mean his dad didn't count anymore.

qa.q: What did Thabo say on Sunday, and why did it help?
qa.a: He apologised for slamming the door and honestly said it felt weird because Sipho wasn't his dad, which let them agree to go slowly.

qa.q: How might Sipho feel when Thabo apologises?
qa.a: Sipho seems relieved and patient, reassuring Thabo that he isn't trying to replace his dad.

grounding: A boy rejects his mother's new partner, fearing he will replace his father; he then stays polite, says honestly how he feels and agrees to go slowly.
